ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the AC voltage source Vs, and on the right side there are two parallel branches connected with this source between the same upper and lower nodes: the middle branch is a series-connected resistor R and inductor L, labeled with current I_RL; the right branch is capacitor C, labeled with current Ic. The text in the figure gives the source voltage Vs = 1∠0 V, and gives the R-L branch current I_RL = √2∠(-π/4) A. Reasoning: Because the series R-L branch is in parallel with the voltage source, the voltage across the two ends of this branch V_RL = Vs = 1∠0 V. According to the complex power formula, the complex power absorbed by the R-L branch is S_RL = V_RL · I_RL* = (1∠0)(√2∠(+π/4)) = √2∠π/4 = 1 + j1 VA. In the R-L branch, the inductor only absorbs reactive power, and only the resistor R consumes real power, therefore the power of resistor R equals the real part of the complex power, 1 W.
